name: Demeclocycline

lead: Demeclocycline is an antibiotic that also makes the kidneys pass more free water, so some users speculate it could cut water retention and puffiness in the face.

As an antibiotic it blocks bacterial protein synthesis; separately, it reduces the collecting duct's response to vasopressin, increasing water loss. Doctors have used that effect off-label for SIADH. No study has tested it for facial puffiness.

paras: It is a prescription capsule or tablet taken as an antibiotic course or, for SIADH, under a doctor's supervision. In depuffing talk it is mentioned for its water-excreting side effect.

The label lists gastrointestinal upset, rare liver toxicity and sun sensitivity, and warns of fetal harm and permanent tooth discoloration in children. Antibiotic use also carries resistance and superinfection concerns. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Demeclocycline appears in depuffing discussions because it makes the kidneys pass more free water, so some users expect less water retention in the face. This aquaretic effect has been used in SIADH. Its use for facial puffiness has not been tested.

lead: Demeclocycline is a semisynthetic tetracycline antibiotic used for infections caused by susceptible organisms such as rickettsiae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia species. Separately, it blunts the kidney's response to antidiuretic hormone, producing an aquaretic effect that has been used off-label in the syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH). [1][2]

It is listed on the wiki under depuffing because of this water-excreting effect. No published study has tested demeclocycline for facial puffiness or any appearance purpose, and no community discussion of it was available to document.
As with other tetracyclines, its label warns of fetal harm in pregnancy and permanent tooth discoloration if used during tooth development in childhood. [2]

paras: The label indicates demeclocycline for rickettsial infections, respiratory infections from Mycoplasma pneumoniae, lymphogranuloma venereum, psittacosis and other infections confirmed or suspected to involve susceptible organisms. [2] Its use for SIADH is not a labelled indication; a 1978 New England Journal of Medicine study compared it with lithium in chronic SIADH. [3]

As an antibiotic, demeclocycline binds the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit and blocks protein synthesis. [1] Grokipedia says it also inhibits the collecting duct's response to ADH, possibly by reducing ADH-induced cAMP and aquaporin-2 channels, increasing free water excretion. [1] The tetracycline group's pharmacokinetics are reviewed in a 2006 article. [4]

The label lists gastrointestinal effects, rare hepatotoxicity, and class warnings that tetracyclines can cause fetal harm and permanent tooth discoloration if used during tooth development. [2] Grokipedia adds photosensitivity and, rarely, pseudotumor cerebri and superinfection. [1]

No studies found on demeclocycline for facial puffiness or cosmetic depuffing. In SIADH, a 1978 NEJM study reported demeclocycline to be superior to lithium in chronic SIADH. [3] Registered trials have examined it for fluorescence delineation of brain tumors. [5]
